prompt.text: Mira shines the same torch first through clear glass and then at a cardboard sheet. Which observation best uses what we know about transparent and opaque materials?

options.label: The cardboard is more likely to make a clear shadow because it blocks the light.
The clear glass must make the darkest shadow because it lets most light pass.
Both must make identical dark shadows because every material blocks all light.
Neither can affect light, so a shadow cannot form.

feedback.correct: Correct. Opaque cardboard blocks light, while transparent glass lets most light pass.
feedback.incorrect: Connect transparency with light passing through and opacity with light being blocked.

prompt.text: A toy car is between Neel and Tara. Neel pushes it away from himself toward Tara. Tara then pulls it toward herself. Which conclusion is best?

options.label: Both actions use force and can change the car's motion, even though one is a push and the other is a pull.
Only Neel uses force because pulling cannot move an object.
Tara's pull must move the car away from her.
Neither action can change motion because the car was already on the floor.

feedback.correct: Correct. Pushes and pulls are forces, and both can change an object's motion.
feedback.incorrect: Use the direction of push and pull, then remember that force can change motion.

prompt.text: Four children want to make less waste at school. Which plan uses reduce, reuse and recycle in the most sensible way?

options.label: Carry a reusable bottle, avoid taking extra disposable items, and put recyclable paper in the correct collection.
Use a new bottle every day and throw paper and plastic into the same bin.
Keep every piece of rubbish forever because reuse means nothing should ever be processed.
Take as many disposable items as possible because recycling means reducing is unnecessary.

feedback.correct: Correct. The plan uses less, uses an item again, and sends suitable material for recycling.
feedback.incorrect: Look for one action that matches each of reduce, reuse and recycle.

prompt.text: A child receives an online message from an unknown person asking for a home address and saying there is an emergency. What is the safest response?

options.label: Do not share the address; show the message to a trusted adult who can decide how to get real help.
Send the address immediately because every message claiming an emergency must be trusted.
Share more personal details first so the sender knows the child is helpful.
Arrange to meet the unknown sender alone to check whether the emergency is real.

feedback.correct: Correct. Safe communication protects personal information and brings a trusted adult into an emergency decision.
feedback.incorrect: Combine safe information sharing with the rule to get trusted adult or emergency-service help.

prompt.text: Two birds are being observed. Bird A has an injured beak but healthy wings. Bird B has a healthy beak but an injured wing. Which prediction best matches the functions of these parts?

options.label: Bird A may have more trouble getting and eating food, while Bird B may have more trouble flying.
Bird A must lose flight because beaks are used for flying, while Bird B cannot eat because wings collect food.
Both injuries must affect only feather colour.
Neither injury can affect the bird because beaks and wings have no useful functions.

feedback.correct: Correct. Beaks help with getting/eating food, while wings help flight in birds that can fly.
feedback.incorrect: Match each body part with its function before comparing the two birds.
